---
title: "Recipes"
engine: markdown
---

Common patterns for documenting terminal workflows. Each recipe is self-contained — copy the fenced block into your own `.qmd` file.

## Interrupt a long-running process

Send Ctrl-C to cancel a command that doesn't terminate on its own. The key is `expect-prompt: false` on the blocking command (since it won't return a prompt) and `literal: false` on the control key (so it's interpreted as a keystroke, not typed literally).

````markdown
```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5
```
````

```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5
```

## Capture a fullscreen TUI

Render the full terminal screen (not just scrollback output). Set `fullscreen: true` on the cell and use `scroll: false` to discard scrollback. End with `expect-prompt: false` so the screen is captured while the app is still displayed.

````markdown
```{term}
#| fullscreen: true
#| scroll: false
cal -y 2026
```
````

```{term}
#| fullscreen: true
#| scroll: false
cal -y 2026
```

For interactive TUIs like `htop` or `less`, end the last command with `expect-prompt: false` and `hold` to capture while still running:

````markdown
```{term}
#| fullscreen: true
#| scroll: false
htop #! expect-prompt: false, hold: 1.0
```
````

## Drive an interactive prompt

Respond to a program that asks questions. Use `expect-prompt: false` on lines that produce a question (not a shell prompt), and provide the answer on the next line.

````markdown
```{term}
read "name?What is your name? " #! expect-prompt: false
World #! expect-prompt: true
echo "Hello, $name!"
```
````

```{term}
read "name?What is your name? " #! expect-prompt: false
World #! expect-prompt: true
echo "Hello, $name!"
```

## Persist state across cells

Each cell runs in the same shell session. Variables, the working directory, and shell state carry over from one cell to the next. This is the key difference from static code blocks.

````markdown
```{term}
PROJECT="my-app"
mkdir -p /tmp/$PROJECT && cd /tmp/$PROJECT
echo "version: 1.0" > config.yml
```

```{term}
pwd
cat config.yml
```
````

```{term}
PROJECT="my-app"
mkdir -p /tmp/$PROJECT && cd /tmp/$PROJECT
echo "version: 1.0" > config.yml
```

```{term}
pwd
cat config.yml
```

## Truncate verbose output

When a command produces many lines but only the shape matters, use `truncate` to collapse a range into a summary. Readers see that output existed without scrolling past it.

````markdown
```{term}
#| truncate: [3:-3]
seq 1 20
```
````

```{term}
#| truncate: [3:-3]
seq 1 20
```

The range `3:-3` keeps the first two and last two lines, replacing everything between with a "[N lines truncated]" message. You can also use regex patterns or multiple ranges.

## Annotate output with callouts

Draw attention to specific lines with numbered callout markers. Use line indices (1-based), negative indices (from end), or regex patterns.

````markdown
```{term}
#| callouts: [2, -1]
echo "start"
echo "important result"
echo "another line"
echo "final output"
```
````

```{term}
#| callouts: [2, -1]
echo "start"
echo "important result"
echo "another line"
echo "final output"
```

## Hide setup, show result

Use `include: false` to run commands that prepare state without showing them in the document. Readers only see the interesting part.

````markdown
```{term}
#| include: false
mkdir -p /tmp/demo-project
echo '{"name": "my-app", "version": "2.1.0"}' > /tmp/demo-project/package.json
echo 'console.log("hello")' > /tmp/demo-project/index.js
```

```{term}
ls /tmp/demo-project/
cat /tmp/demo-project/package.json | python3 -m json.tool
```
````

```{term}
#| include: false
mkdir -p /tmp/demo-project
echo '{"name": "my-app", "version": "2.1.0"}' > /tmp/demo-project/package.json
echo 'console.log("hello")' > /tmp/demo-project/index.js
```

```{term}
ls /tmp/demo-project/
cat /tmp/demo-project/package.json | python3 -m json.tool
```

## Remove noise from output

Strip specific lines that clutter the output — warnings, empty lines, or headers you don't want. Unlike `truncate`, removed lines disappear entirely with no placeholder.

````markdown
```{term}
#| remove: ["^$"]
echo "first"
echo ""
echo "second"
echo ""
echo "third"
```
````

```{term}
#| remove: ["^$"]
echo "first"
echo ""
echo "second"
echo ""
echo "third"
```

## Simulate realistic typing

Add human-like typing cadence for screencasts or demos. Typing simulation adds random per-character delays so commands appear one keystroke at a time.

````markdown
```{term}
#| typing: true
echo "This looks like a human typed it"
```
````

```{term}
#| typing: true
echo "This looks like a human typed it"
```

## Control arrow keys and navigation

Use `literal: false` to send special keys — arrows, tab, escape sequences. Space-separated words on one line are sent as individual keystrokes.

````markdown
```{term}
echo "first command"
echo "second command"
up up enter #! literal: false, delay: 0.3
```
````

```{term}
echo "first command"
echo "second command"
up up enter #! literal: false, delay: 0.3
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -rf /tmp/demo-project /tmp/my-app
```
